IMAP protocol support

maild serves IMAP over implicit TLS. Sessions start in IMAP4rev1 compatibility mode; ENABLE IMAP4rev2 switches to rev2 responses and UTF-8 mailbox names. ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT enables UTF-8 while retaining rev1 SEARCH responses. Rev1 mailbox names use modified UTF-7, including &- for a literal ampersand. Non-canonical shifts, including shifted printable ASCII, fail with BAD. CREATE, RENAME and subscriptions share Net-Unicode character validation, including C1 control rejection. Explicit CHARSET US-ASCII and CHARSET UTF-8 work in every SEARCH mode.

The selected-read cost test uses 10,000 messages and 1,000 single-message FETCHes, counting native store calls. It also checks 100 IDLE flag events without relisting the mailbox and one catch-up diff for an unknown UID. Ordinary notifications use the mailbox's native change counter, including flag changes and removals.

Contiguous requested UID runs use one membership-index range scan each. Full-folder FETCH uses one scan even when expunges left UID holes. A transient IDLE snapshot failure produces UNAVAILABLE and preserves the session and its view for retry on the next event. The wire regression also counts full-folder and sparse FETCH scans and injects a failed IDLE catch-up before retrying it.

selected_imap_view_observes_cross_session_jmap_smtp_and_sieve_changes selects a mailbox, performs unchanged FETCHes, then checks NOOP notifications after other IMAP sessions append and expunge, JMAP Email/set changes memberships, SMTP delivers mail, and Sieve files SMTP mail into the selected mailbox. Account deletion is also tested through the application and property-store SQLite connections: both enable foreign keys and cascade Sieve scripts, versions and vacation stamps.

SAVE failures clear $, including grammar errors. Successful DELETE of the selected mailbox returns to authenticated state, with CLOSED in rev2. Missing subscription rows carry both NonExistent and Noselect; subscription-only children use CHILDINFO without changing a live mailbox's HasChildren attribute. The empty LIST pattern remains a delimiter probe when RETURN options are present, and LIST-STATUS APPENDLIMIT uses the session configuration.

SEARCH scans decoded MIME content without making whole-message lowercased copies. Its substring matcher uses linear work and memory proportional to the needle. Content-dependent searches refuse messages above the 64 MiB work limit with NO [LIMIT]; they do not return incomplete matches. A query-weighted 256 MiB scan budget also bounds repeated predicates against one message (repeated_content_searches_share_a_per_message_work_budget). Metadata-only searches can still match these messages. Unreadable content produces NO [UNAVAILABLE].

Binary APPEND preserves decoded body octets while storing NUL-bearing leaf parts with base64 transfer encoding. This keeps ordinary BODY responses valid IMAP strings; BINARY returns the original decoded octets. Unsupported binary encodings or NUL in message headers fail with UNKNOWN-CTE. UTF8=ACCEPT also supports the UTF8 (~{N}...) APPEND form. Embedded-message reparsing shares a 64-level budget across binary APPEND normalisation (binary_append_bounds_reparsed_message_nesting). BINARY accepts both padded and unpadded MIME base64. RFC822 and RFC822.TEXT set Seen; RFC822.HEADER and read-only FETCHes do not. RENAME INBOX retains each membership's flags and user keywords.

Capabilities come from an implementation allowlist. Operator overrides can select a subset but cannot add unimplemented extensions. APPENDLIMIT always comes from imap_max_literal_bytes. LITERAL+ permits non-synchronising literals up to the configured cap; a LITERAL- override limits non-synchronising literals to 4096 octets while permitting larger synchronising literals. Command-wide allocation and literal-count limits apply as well. Input that cannot be safely drained closes the connection instead of being interpreted as new commands. The two protocol capabilities remain present even with an operator override.

Original refusal inventory

These are the refusal sites found before implementation. Comments and tests containing the same wording are included so an obsolete phase note cannot be mistaken for a remaining protocol limit.

Original site under services/maild/src/imap/Resolution

codec.rs: unstripped literal refusal; mid-command literal refusal; SEARCH-only multi-literal documentationGeneral segmented session framing, retaining bounded refusal and FramingLost paths
op/fetch.rs: part-addressing deferrals, BODY refusal and macro refusalsMIME traversal, non-extensible BODY and macro expansion
op/search.rs: SEARCH RETURN refusalESEARCH and session SEARCHRES state
op/status.rs: SIZE/DELETED deferrals and unsupported-item rejectionMembership aggregates and APPENDLIMIT; unknown items still fail
op/list.rs: non-empty reference and extension-option refusalsExtended parser, reference resolution and LIST-STATUS
op/lsub.rs: non-empty reference refusalSame reference resolution as LIST
op/rename.rs: INBOX deferralAtomic storage operation retaining the INBOX container
op/store.rs: user keywords described as deferredDocumentation corrected; per-membership keywords remain supported
op/create.rs: transactional parent-walk deferralParent creation remains incremental; message operations use atomic transactions. A failed leaf creation may leave newly created parents, which a retry reuses
op/select.rs: CONDSTORE/QRESYNC parameter refusal; op/fetch.rs: MODSEQ refusal; op/store.rs: UNCHANGEDSINCE deferralIntentional dependency on the complete imap-ext implementation; not advertised or enabled here

op/check.rs: “deferred mailbox state”; session.rs: matching CHECK commentDescriptive only: CHECK has no pending storage work to flush
session.rs: unknown UID inner command and generic phase refusalInvalid commands remain BAD; all standard UID subcommands are dispatched
session.rs: STARTTLS refusalExplicit implicit-TLS-only policy; no cleartext IMAP listener is offered

Additional RFC 9051 audit findings

The audit also checked server requirements beyond the refusal strings:

Requirement groupFinding and resolution
Sections 4, 5.1 and Appendix A: strings and namesAdded UTF-8 negotiation, modified UTF-7 compatibility, NFC validation and literal-kind tracking
Sections 2.3.1.1 and 6.3.4: recreated mailbox identityPersistent UIDVALIDITY high-water mark for new mailboxes, seeded from current wire identities and time. Legacy millisecond values convert to their existing seconds value, preserving client caches. RENAME allocates a fresh value only for a renamed mailbox whose identity collides with another live mailbox or a recorded retired value. DELETE and collision repair retain old values, protecting earlier cached names after rename-away/delete sequences. legacy_identities_migrate_before_login_and_cannot_collide_after_rename and rename_repairs_only_colliding_live_or_deleted_name_identities cover both paths
Sections 5.2 and 7.5.1: mailbox updates and MSN stabilityAdded command-time refresh and preserved views while expunge notifications are prohibited
Sections 6.3.2–6.3.3: selection data and read-only flagsAccurate LIST attributes and OLDNAME in rev2; CLOSED boundaries on reselection, including failed SELECT; RECENT/UNSEEN in rev1; empty PERMANENTFLAGS for EXAMINE. Covered by rev2_reselection_marks_the_closed_boundary_including_failure and examine_fetch_and_close_unselect_have_distinct_effects
Section 6.3.4: existing mailbox creationCorrected old idempotent CREATE INBOX and CREATE existing/ behaviour to NO
Sections 6.3.5–6.3.8: mailbox lifecycleDELETE removes memberships atomically, protects children and INBOX; subscription names persist
Sections 6.3.12 and 6.4.7: mutation failureAdded atomic MULTIAPPEND and COPY, including UID allocation rollback
Sections 6.4.1–6.4.2: CLOSE and UNSELECTCorrected CLOSE’s missing expunge; UNSELECT remains non-expunging
Sections 6.4.4–6.4.5 and 7.5.2: search and body dataAdded ESEARCH, SAVE lifetime, charset handling, body forms, encoded sections and decoded binary sizes
Sections 6.1.3, 7.1 and 7.2: responsesFinal capability list after authentication; operational UNAVAILABLE errors; shutdown BYE
Sections 6.4.8–6.4.9: MOVE and UIDPLUSRetained COPYUID-before-EXPUNGE ordering, UID EXPUNGE filtering and implicit UID FETCH items

UID ordering, immutable message identities, authentication, NAMESPACE, UNSELECT, literal abuse caps and the existing MOVE/UIDPLUS behaviours retain their original regression suites. The release tests are necessary evidence; this document does not claim certification by every mail client.

CONDSTORE, QRESYNC, MODSEQ, UNCHANGEDSINCE and STATUS HIGHESTMODSEQ are integration hooks for work/maild-imap-ext. ENABLE ignores those names and omits an empty ENABLED response until that complete implementation lands. STARTTLS remains refused under the implicit TLS policy.

Protocol references: RFC 9051, BINARY, ENABLE, SEARCHRES, LIST-EXTENDED, UTF8=ACCEPT, APPENDLIMIT.
